skill.name: when-analyzing-performance-use-performance-analysis
skill.description: Analyze Claude Flow swarm performance with baselines, profiling, bottleneck classification, optimization planning, and validation guidance.
skill.summary: Guides structured Claude Flow swarm performance analysis from baseline to validation.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: The static backtick and command-substitution findings are mostly Markdown examples or safe shell expressions. A real risk remains because the skill directs runtime npx execution from the alpha channel and includes state-changing optimization commands.

remediation.issue: Runtime npx execution from a mutable alpha package
remediation.suggestion: Pin Claude Flow to a reviewed version and require user confirmation before running npx commands.
Replace auto-apply examples with dry-run commands and documented approval steps.

remediation.issue: Shell examples assume trusted generated identifiers and files
remediation.suggestion: Validate agent IDs, keep output paths inside a known directory, and quote all file inputs.

semantic_findings.title: Runtime External Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill repeatedly directs users or agents to run npx claude-flow@alpha. This downloads and executes mutable package code at runtime.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands are explicit and repeated across the main workflow. The alpha tag is mutable, so the executed package can change after review.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic State-Changing Optimization
semantic_findings.description: The workflow includes auto-apply optimization, topology changes, agent rebalancing, memory cleanup, and neural training commands. These can change swarm state without clear approval gates.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited commands are explicit state-changing operations. The skill presents them as workflow steps rather than requiring a dry run or separate approval.

content.value_statement: Performance work is hard when swarm metrics, profiles, and benchmarks are scattered. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured analysis workflow.
actual_capabilities: Establishes baseline metrics for Claude Flow swarms.
Profiles swarm execution, agents, memory, CPU, and network behavior.
Classifies bottlenecks by severity and likely impact.
Guides optimization planning for topology, allocation, caching, and memory use.
Validates improvements with comparison benchmarks and target checks.
limitations: Requires Claude Flow and related shell tools to be installed.
Uses command examples that need review before execution.
Assumes expected JSON output from the Claude Flow CLI.
Does not independently verify results from external profiling tools.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Slow Swarm Workflows
use_cases.description: Find likely bottlenecks when a Claude Flow swarm has poor throughput or high latency.

use_cases.title: Validate Optimization Results
use_cases.description: Compare baseline and optimized runs to show whether performance targets were reached.

use_cases.title: Prepare Repeatable Benchmarks
use_cases.description: Create a consistent performance workflow for profiling, reporting, and regression checks.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to establish a baseline for my Claude Flow swarm. Summarize throughput, latency, resource use, and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Profile a Slow Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to profile a Claude Flow workflow with slow task completion. Identify likely CPU, memory, network, and coordination bottlenecks.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Optimization Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare baseline and optimized benchmark results. Rank bottlenecks and recommend changes with validation metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Full Improvement Cycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill for a full performance improvement cycle on a production-like swarm. Require approval before any state-changing optimization command.

output_examples.input: A swarm completes tasks slowly after adding more agents.
output_examples.output: The result identifies coordination overhead, slow agent response times, and a benchmark plan. It recommends topology changes and post-change validation.

output_examples.input: A team needs to prove an optimization improved performance.
output_examples.output: The result compares baseline and current metrics, reports throughput and latency deltas, and lists whether improvement targets were met.

output_examples.input: Memory usage grows during long swarm workflows.
output_examples.output: The result summarizes memory hotspots, likely leaks, affected agents, and safe profiling steps before any cleanup command.

best_practices: Establish a baseline before changing topology, memory settings, or agent allocation.
Review every generated shell command before running it in a shared environment.
Validate changes with repeated benchmarks and compare results against explicit targets.
anti_patterns: Do not auto-apply optimizations before reviewing recommendations and rollback steps.
Do not compare results from different workload sizes or measurement windows.
Do not treat profiler output as complete without checking logs and error rates.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes Claude Flow swarm performance, including baselines, profiles, bottlenecks, optimizations, and validation results.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: It provides command workflows for an AI agent or user to review. Users should approve commands before execution.

faq.question: Which tools does it require?
faq.answer: It expects Claude Flow and standard shell tools, including jq and bc for some examples.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow can guide Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when shell access is available.

faq.question: Does it change my swarm configuration?
faq.answer: Some examples can change topology, memory, and agent allocation. Run those only after review.

faq.question: How should I use results?
faq.answer: Use results to prioritize bottlenecks, choose changes, and confirm improvements with repeated benchmarks.
